name: semver
headline_counts: downloads in the last 30 days (the npm/dm badge)

components.label: Lockfile replays (CI, containers)
components.assumption: A fresh `npm install` resolves the newest version of a compatibility line. Downloads of an older version in the same line come from a package-lock being replayed, and a developer machine caches packages, so a repeat download of a pinned version is a CI runner or container starting cold. npm only publishes per-version counts for the last 7 days; that split is applied to the whole window. A version superseded inside those 7 days counts as fresh.

components.label: Pinned old line with no published dependent
components.assumption: An older compatibility line that no published package requires is being pulled by projects that never publish: one app's or one company's CI. It is a handful of consumers, not a crowd. Only applied when the dependents for that line were counted.

components.label: Release-time fetches (mirrors, scanners, update bots)
components.assumption: On a publish day and the 1 day(s) after, downloads above the median of the 7 quiet days before are mirrors, registries, scanners and Dependabot/Renovate fetching the new version, not new users. 3 release(s) in the window. When release days cover more than 40% of the window there is no quiet baseline and nothing is removed here.

components.label: Flat automation (same every day of the week)
components.assumption: People work weekdays. Human-driven traffic on a weekend day is 0.48x a weekday (measured, see README). Whatever does not follow that rhythm is cron jobs, scheduled CI and bots: 4436004 a day here. Push-triggered CI follows the human week and is NOT removed by this step.

components.label: Human-rhythm fresh resolves (the real part, upper bound)
components.assumption: What is left: newest-in-line downloads on quiet days that follow the working week. It still includes push-triggered CI that resolves without a lockfile, so it is an upper bound on people.

components.label: Lockfile replays (CI, containers)
components.assumption: A fresh `npm install` resolves the newest version of a compatibility line. Downloads of an older version in the same line come from a package-lock being replayed, and a developer machine caches packages, so a repeat download of a pinned version is a CI runner or container starting cold. npm only publishes per-version counts for the last 7 days; that split is applied to the whole window. A version superseded inside those 7 days counts as fresh.

components.label: Pinned old line with no published dependent
components.assumption: An older compatibility line that no published package requires is being pulled by projects that never publish: one app's or one company's CI. It is a handful of consumers, not a crowd. Only applied when the dependents for that line were counted.

components.label: Release-time fetches (mirrors, scanners, update bots)
components.assumption: On a publish day and the 1 day(s) after, downloads above the median of the 7 quiet days before are mirrors, registries, scanners and Dependabot/Renovate fetching the new version, not new users. 12 release(s) in the window. When release days cover more than 40% of the window there is no quiet baseline and nothing is removed here.

components.label: Flat automation (same every day of the week)
components.assumption: People work weekdays. Human-driven traffic on a weekend day is 0.48x a weekday (measured, see README). Whatever does not follow that rhythm is cron jobs, scheduled CI and bots: 1118848 a day here. Push-triggered CI follows the human week and is NOT removed by this step.
